facts.raw_span: A man in his 70s
history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, and moderate pulmonary hypertension
presented with shortness of breath, increased abdominal girth, and bilateral leg swelling
recurrent palpitations that occurred randomly and were often associated with shortness of breath
Left ventricular ejection fraction of 40% compared with 60% 2 months prior
25% narrowing of the left anterior descending artery and a distally occluded right coronary artery
Regular narrow complex supraventricular tachycardia with rate of 120 beats per minute
subtle retrograde P waves during tachyarrhythmia
aspirin, atorvastatin, amlodipine, tiotropium, and a budesonide-formoterol inhaler
No specific physical examination findings were detailed in the case report
